title: `mean` and `median` of integers: `Float64`
verdict: a double: the `Float64` sum over the count
description: `mean` of integers is a `Float64` (the values cast to doubles and summed, polars-sum-float), so it rounds above 2⁵³ (`mean(2⁶², 2⁶², 1)` is 3.0744573456182584e18). `median` of integers is a `Float64` too. Both are NULL for no values.

Every integer width takes one generic path (`with_match_physical_numeric_polars_type`, `T: PolarsIntegerType`): each value becomes an `f64`, exactly for 8 to 32 bits, and the sum is an `f64`: pairwise ungrouped, Kahan per group in memory, value by value per group when streaming. A sum below 2⁵³ is exact in any order, so for `Int8` to `Int32` the mean is the exact quotient rounded once on either engine. Above 2⁵³ (`Int64`) the engines can round the sum differently.
reference: `avg` of `i64` returns `i64` in Substrait; the reference follows the declared output type (`avg_int_result`, #209).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `sum_arr_as_f64` converts each integer to `f64` (`as_`) and sums pairwise
in-memory grouped mean of integers: `KahanSum` of `to_f64` values, `Float64` result
streaming: one `NumMeanReducer` per physical numeric type, `Float64` output for integers
